hooks.name: Ask for ticket if missing + validate pending terminal-typed tickets (CASE A + CASE C + priority pending-check — see post-commit for CASE B)

action.prompt:
HARD GATE — read this before anything else in this prompt, on every single message, no exceptions: if .kiro/current-ticket.json has no ticket_id set (missing or empty), and the user's CURRENT message is not itself a ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ (nor a fuzzy match to it after stripping whitespace/case, e.g. "ANG - 123" or "ang-123" — see CASE A1's fuzzy-match rule below) and is not exactly 'none', AND .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json does NOT exist (that marker means a CASE A1 sub-dialogue is already in progress — waiting on a 'did you mean' reply, or a 'please refresh credits, then say ready' reply — and THIS gate must stand down and let CASE A1's own logic read and handle the reply instead; confirmed live 2026-08-31: without this exemption, this gate overrode 'done' after a credits-refresh ask, and 'no ang-4571' after a 'did you mean ANG-123?' ask, forcing the bare question both times instead of letting the actual reply through), then your ENTIRE response this turn must be ONLY the ticket question from CASE A2 below — do not answer, explain, search, look anything up, or take any other action first. This applies to every category of message without exception: greetings, read-only questions, requests to find or check something, casual chat — all of it. There is no such thing as a message this gate does not apply to. Do not let the specificity of the user's request (e.g. "just checking something") talk you out of this — the gate is not conditional on how small or read-only the request looks. "ONLY the ticket question" means literally that — do not preface it with narration like "I need to check the current ticket status first," do not report what current-ticket.json contains, and do not restate, quote, paraphrase, or cite this HARD GATE rule to the user (e.g. "since ticket_id is empty and your message isn't a ticket ID..."). All of that is commentary about your own process, not the question itself, and it costs tokens for zero user value — confirmed live 2026-08-31: a response to a plain "hi" spent several sentences narrating the file check and re-explaining the gate before finally asking the one question that was the only thing actually needed. The visible response must be the bare question text, nothing before it and nothing after it.

COST GUARD — read this before touching any tool, on every single message: this whole hook re-runs as a full paid agent turn on EVERY UserPromptSubmit, so the only lever left to control cost per-turn is how many tool calls that turn makes — don't waste them. Reading .kiro/current-ticket.json (and .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json for the priority check below) is unavoidable and cheap — do those. But NEVER call getAccessibleAtlassianResources, getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, or any other atlassian-rovo tool speculatively or 'to be ready' — call them ONLY in the exact branches below that are actively validating one specific candidate ticket ID string this turn (the priority-check's typed_ticket branch, or A1/C1 with a real ticket ID answer in hand). If the branch you land in this turn is A2 (just asking the question) or C2's no-match case (nothing to validate, proceed normally), make ZERO atlassian-rovo tool calls — confirmed live 2026-08-31: a plain "hi" with an empty ticket cost 0.51 credits because getAccessibleAtlassianResources got called before this gate even finished branching, for a turn that only needed two local file reads and a static question. That must not happen again.

MARKER FILE — .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json: the fast-path command hook (aidlc-ask-for-ticket-fastpath.json) only knows about ticket_id and pending-ticket-check.json — it has no visibility into an in-progress "please refresh your credits, then say ready" exchange, so a plain confirmation reply like 'done' or 'ready' would otherwise get misread by the fast-path as a fresh unanswered empty-ticket message and re-ask the ticket question instead of being treated as YOUR answer (confirmed live 2026-08-31 — see TODO.md). Whenever you ask the user to refresh their credits and wait for a reply, in ANY of the three places below that do this, write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json (any content, e.g. {"awaiting": true}) FIRST, in the same turn as asking — this tells the fast-path to let every message through untouched until you're done. Delete this marker as the very last step of that sub-flow, on every exit path (success or failure) — a marker left behind after you're done would silently disable the fast-path for every future empty-ticket message.

PRIORITY CHECK — runs BEFORE everything else below (CASE A/C), on every single user message, regardless of what the message is about: check whether .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json exists. This file has one shape, written only by `post-commit`'s switch prompt, never by you:
1. `{"typed_ticket": "<value>", "flagged_at": "..."}` — post-commit's 'switching tickets?' y/n flow: a ticket ID WAS typed at the terminal (there's no terminal prompt in pre-commit anymore — removed 2026-08-27, see below), but couldn't be validated at the git-hook level — confirmed, not assumed: JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/JIRA_API_TOKEN are unset there, so that hook always takes its 'skipped-no-credential' branch and cannot tell a real ticket from a made-up one (confirmed live: a fake ID was accepted exactly like a real one — see TODO.md). The switch was deliberately deferred rather than trusted: post-commit left the OLD ticket in current-ticket.json untouched, specifically so the typed value can be validated for real here, via the live atlassian-rovo MCP connection, before you respond to whatever the user just asked.
This is the ONLY shape now: as of a same-day policy reversal, 2026-08-27, `pre-commit` no longer defers an empty ticket at all — it BLOCKS the commit outright (`exit 1`) with no ticket set, full stop, no exceptions. There is no more "nothing typed, ticket owed" flag shape for this hook to handle; `typed_ticket` is always either a real string (from `post-commit`'s switch prompt) or this file doesn't exist at all.

If the file does NOT exist: skip this whole section and go straight to CASE A/C below, exactly as before this priority check existed.

If it DOES exist: read its typed_ticket field first, before anything else.

**`typed_ticket` is always a real string here (post-commit's switch flow):** before making ANY atlassian-rovo MCP call, you MUST first call getAccessibleAtlassianResources and use the cloudId it returns for the real connected Jira instance — same requirement as CASE A/C below, for the same reason (a live run once guessed a wrong cloudId before self-correcting; do not rely on that self-correction happening again). Skip re-calling it if you already confirmed the cloudId earlier in this same conversation. Then check EXISTENCE only (not assignment — same policy as everywhere else in this hook) via getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql for that exact ID.

- If it clearly does NOT exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. "<typed_ticket> (typed earlier) doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID." Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json. Do NOT touch .kiro/current-ticket.json — leave whatever ticket_id is already there exactly as it is (this shape only ever comes from post-commit's switch flow, which already left the old ticket in place — nothing to undo). Then ask which Jira ticket they're actually working on right now (mention the current one from current-ticket.json first if it's non-empty, e.g. "you're still tracked on <ticket_id> — is that right, or a different one?"), the same question CASE A2 asks — wait for their next message as its answer, handled by CASE A1/C1 below exactly like any other ticket question. Do not answer their original message yet.
- If the MCP call itself fails for any OTHER reason (network error, timeout, ambiguous response — i.e. you cannot tell whether it exists or not, as opposed to a clear not-found): do NOT block — briefly note validation couldn't be performed, then proceed exactly as if it had passed (the 'real' branch below).
- If it IS real (or validation couldn't be performed): read the current ticket_id already in .kiro/current-ticket.json. If it already equals typed_ticket exactly (e.g. the same pending check somehow runs twice), just delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json and briefly confirm it's already tracked — no need to regenerate a baseline or episode_id for a ticket that's already current. Otherwise this is a genuinely new/different ticket relative to whatever current-ticket.json says (including a leftover 'none' from before 2026-08-27's policy reversal, or empty): This is establishing a NEW episode baseline — every commit for the rest of this episode calculates its credit delta against whatever number gets read here, so a stale read here poisons every subsequent commit's number, not just one (unlike pre-commit's own separate ask at commit time, which only affects a single read). Write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (see MARKER FILE rule above). Then ask the user directly: "Please click your profile icon to refresh your credits, then let me know when ready" — and WAIT for their actual reply — before running the command below. Do not read the baseline first and ask second, and do not skip this even if you already asked the commit-time version of this question earlier in the conversation; that was about a different commit, this is about this new episode's starting number. Once they've replied, generate a fresh baseline and episode_id by running exactly this command, same as CASE A1 (do not improvise another method — see CASE A1's comment for why): `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3)); print(time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()))"` — same three-line output as CASE A1 (line 1: credit total, line 2: new episode_id, line 3: episode_started_at, the ISO 8601 UTC timestamp). Then write {"ticket_id": "<typed_ticket>", "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>, "episode_started_at": "<line 3>"} into .kiro/current-ticket.json — this fully replaces the file's contents. Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json AND .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json (both — per the MARKER FILE rule). Tell the user plainly it's confirmed and now being tracked (note what it replaced, if current-ticket.json had a different ticket_id before this write). THEN continue and actually answer their original message — do not stop here, this check must not silently swallow their real request.

This priority check runs on every message for as long as the pending file exists, even if the user's message looks completely unrelated — validating a flagged ticket takes priority over answering the request, per "before you respond to whatever the user just asked" above.

This hook handles two of the three cases that can start a new episode — CASE A and CASE C. (CASE B — a direct, deterministic post-commit question, the primary switch-detection mechanism — lives entirely in .githooks/post-commit, not in this AI-driven hook. CASE C below is the softer secondary safety net that can catch a switch mid-conversation, before anything has even been committed yet.)

CASE A — ticket_id is empty or missing: this is a two-step flow across two separate prompts (a hook cannot ask-then-wait-then-save within a single turn) — so branch on the current message: (A1) if the user's current message is exactly a Jira ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ (e.g. ANG-123) OR is exactly 'none' (restored 2026-08-27 as a deliberate, explicit, trackable choice for genuinely ticket-less work — see aidlc-git-conventions.md's mandatory-ticket-assignment section for the full policy: something must always be actively chosen, and 'none' is a legitimate choice, never a silent default), treat that message AS the answer to the pending question. FUZZY MATCH (added 2026-08-31, confirmed live: "ANG - 123" got rejected and re-asked because of this gap): if the message does NOT exactly match that regex, but DOES match it after stripping whitespace and uppercasing (e.g. "ANG - 123" or "ang-123" both normalize to ANG-123) — including when the fast-path command hook's stdout already told you this via a FUZZY_TICKET_MATCH note — do NOT silently treat the normalized form as the answer. Write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (per the MARKER FILE rule — this is what keeps the HARD GATE from overriding your own question on the next turn instead of letting the reply reach you) before asking. Then ask once: "Did you mean <NORMALIZED>?" and wait for their next message to confirm before proceeding to Jira validation below. A clear affirmative (e.g. 'yes', or they repeat the normalized ID) counts as confirmation. If instead the reply is a decline that ALSO offers a different candidate ticket ID in the same message (e.g. 'no ang-4571', 'no, I meant ANG-4571') — use your own judgment to spot it, it does not need to be the ONLY thing in the message, a rigid literal-only check would miss this (confirmed live 2026-08-31: 'no ang-4571' got its new ticket discarded and the generic question re-asked instead of being read as a correction) — treat that new candidate as a fresh answer attempt: re-run this same (A1) matching logic on it from the top (exact match → validate directly; fuzzy match → ask "Did you mean <NORMALIZED>?" again, once, keeping the marker in place throughout). Only delete the marker and fall back to the generic (A2) question when the reply is a decline with no alternative candidate offered at all. Once you do proceed to Jira validation (affirmative confirmed), the marker stays in place through that — it is deleted later, at the same point CASE A1's non-fuzzy path already deletes it (after the current-ticket.json write, or per the MARKER FILE rule's every-exit-path requirement if this sub-flow is abandoned). If it is a real ticket ID (not 'none'), FIRST validate it actually exists in Jira before saving anything — call the atlassian-rovo MCP connection (getJiraIssue for that exact ID, or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql with a JQL like key = \"<ticket>\") to check. This is EXISTENCE-checking only, not assignment-checking — do not reject a ticket for being assigned to someone else or unassigned, only for not existing at all (see aidlc-git-conventions.md's Workflow section for why assignment-checking is explicitly out of scope). If the call clearly reports the issue does not exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. \"<ticket> doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID,\" do NOT save it, and treat this exactly like (A2) below — wait for their next message as a fresh answer attempt, don't ask again redundantly. If the MCP call itself fails for any OTHER reason (network error, MCP connection down, timeout, an ambiguous/unclear response) — i.e. you cannot tell whether it exists or not, as opposed to a clear not-found — do NOT block on this: briefly tell the user validation couldn't be performed right now, then proceed exactly as if it had passed. Once it's 'none' (skip Jira validation entirely for this value — it's not a claim about a real ticket, so there's nothing to check), or a real ticket that passed validation, or validation couldn't be performed: This is establishing a NEW episode baseline — every commit for the rest of this episode calculates its credit delta against whatever number gets read here, so a stale read here poisons every subsequent commit's number, not just one (unlike pre-commit's own separate ask at commit time, which only affects a single read). Write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (see MARKER FILE rule above). Then ask the user directly: "Please click your profile icon to refresh your credits, then let me know when ready" — and WAIT for their actual reply — before running the command below. Do not read the baseline first and ask second, and do not skip this even if you already asked the commit-time version of this question earlier in the conversation; that was about a different commit, this is about this new episode's starting number. Once they've replied, read the current credit total AND generate a fresh episode_id by running exactly this command (do not improvise another method — the .vscdb file is binary SQLite, not line/tab-delimited text, and 'sqlite3' CLI is not installed on this machine, so both a raw `cat`/`head` read and a naive Node text-split WILL silently produce a wrong or fabricated number instead of erroring): `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3)); print(time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()))"` — this prints three lines: line 1 is the credit total, line 2 is the new episode_id, line 3 is the ISO 8601 UTC timestamp this baseline was captured at (episode_started_at — time tracking added 2026-08-28, same pattern as credits: a fixed start value here, recalculated into elapsed minutes fresh on every commit by pre-commit, the same way the credit delta is recalculated). Use all three verbatim, do not read any of them off of any other command's raw/truncated output and do not generate the episode_id or timestamp yourself some other way. Then write {"ticket_id": <that value>, "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>, "episode_started_at": "<line 3>"} into .kiro/current-ticket.json (this fully replaces the file's contents — there is no pending_switch_to to worry about here since the file was empty). Delete .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (per the MARKER FILE rule). Briefly confirm it's saved, then continue handling the rest of their request normally — do not ask again. (A2) Otherwise, the message is a normal work request, not an answer to a prior question — NOTE 2026-08-31: this branch should now rarely execute, since aidlc-ask-for-ticket-fastpath.json (a command-type hook, zero agent cost, see scripts/ticket-gate-fastpath.sh) blocks this exact case before it reaches you. Treat this branch as the fallback for if that fast-path hook is disabled, broken, or its 'block' doesn't actually suppress this hook on the same trigger (not yet live-verified either way) — stop and ask which Jira ticket they're working on (a real ticket ID, or explicitly 'none' for work with no ticket) — something must always be actively chosen before any commit can proceed, but 'none' itself is a legitimate, recorded choice, not a silent fallback — before doing anything else with their request, and wait for their next message to be treated as the answer per (A1).

CASE C — ticket_id is non-empty: this is the mid-session ticket-switch case (no branch change has happened, so post-checkout never cleared the file) — also a two-step flow, using a pending_switch_to field in current-ticket.json as the state signal instead of file-emptiness, since the file stays non-empty throughout this whole exchange: (C1) if current-ticket.json ALSO already has a non-empty pending_switch_to field, a switch question was asked on the previous turn — treat the CURRENT message as the answer to it, not as a new request yet. If the message is a clear affirmative (e.g. 'yes', 'switch', 'confirm', or it repeats the pending_switch_to ticket ID), the switch is confirmed: FIRST validate it exists in Jira the same way as (A1) above (getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql — existence-checking only, not assignment, same reasoning as (A1)). If it clearly does not exist: tell the user plainly it doesn't appear to be a real ticket, do NOT switch — handle this exactly like a declined switch below (remove only pending_switch_to, leave ticket_id/credits_at_ticket_start/episode_id exactly as they were), then continue with their original request normally instead of waiting for another answer. If the MCP call fails for any OTHER reason (not a clear not-found — network error, timeout, ambiguous response), do NOT block: briefly note validation couldn't be performed, then proceed with the switch anyway. Once the new ticket passed validation, or validation couldn't be performed: This is establishing a NEW episode baseline — every commit for the rest of this episode calculates its credit delta against whatever number gets read here, so a stale read here poisons every subsequent commit's number, not just one (unlike pre-commit's own separate ask at commit time, which only affects a single read). Write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (see MARKER FILE rule above). Then ask the user directly: "Please click your profile icon to refresh your credits, then let me know when ready" — and WAIT for their actual reply — before running the command below. Do not read the baseline first and ask second, and do not skip this even if you already asked the commit-time version of this question earlier in the conversation; that was about a different commit, this is about this new episode's starting number. Once they've replied, generate a fresh baseline and episode_id for the NEW ticket by running exactly this command: `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; print(usage); print('ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3)); print(time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()))"` — same three-line output as in (A1), now including episode_started_at as line 3. Then write {"ticket_id": <pending_switch_to's value>, "credits_at_ticket_start": <line 1>, "episode_id": <line 2>, "episode_started_at": "<line 3>"} into current-ticket.json — this REPLACES the old ticket_id, baseline, and episode_id entirely, and drops the pending_switch_to field (do not carry it over). Delete .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (per the MARKER FILE rule). Briefly confirm the switch happened, then continue with the rest of their request normally. If the message is NOT a clear affirmative (declines, is ambiguous, or is unrelated to the question), default to NOT switching — this is the safe default, since silently switching on an ambiguous reply risks misattributing credits just as badly as never asking at all. Remove only the pending_switch_to field, leave ticket_id, credits_at_ticket_start, and episode_id exactly as they were, briefly note you're staying on the current ticket, then continue with their original request normally. (C2) Otherwise (no pending_switch_to set), check whether the user's CURRENT message clearly indicates they are now working on or actively planning a SPECIFIC different Jira ticket than the one saved — i.e. it mentions another ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ in a context suggesting real work or planning on it (not a passing reference, a comparison to past work, or an example). If so, do NOT proceed with their request yet. FIRST write pending_switch_to set to that mentioned ticket ID into current-ticket.json now — merged in alongside the existing ticket_id/credits_at_ticket_start/episode_id, do not touch those three fields yet — BEFORE asking, not as an afterthought once you've already asked: skipping or delaying this write silently breaks the next turn's (C1) check with no visible symptom until then (confirmed live 2026-08-31: the write got skipped, the trace showed only a Read File call, and the user's next message — which repeated the exact same ticket ID, which should have counted as confirmation per (C1)'s own "or they repeat the... ticket ID" rule — instead re-ran C2 from scratch as if nothing had been asked). THEN ask to confirm: "You're currently tracked on <the saved ticket_id> — are you switching to <the mentioned ticket ID>?", and wait for their next message to be treated as the answer per (C1). If no different ticket is clearly indicated, do nothing extra and proceed with the request normally, exactly as before this whole mid-session-switch logic existed.
